build_context.description:
A palaia memory vault.

Assemble the context around a starting point: resolve it, walk its relations to `depth` hops, and return one deduplicated, token-budgeted package. This is the 'continue where we left off' tool — it follows the links the notes actually declare instead of re-searching. Notes that do not fit `max_tokens` are shortened to their title plus key facts, never cut mid-note. `depth` is capped at 5; `timeframe` ('30d', '2w', or an ISO date) keeps the walk to what is still current.

depth.description: Relation hops to walk from the starting point, 0-5. 1 is 'this note and what it names'.

max_tokens.description: Token budget for the whole package. Notes that do not fit are summarized, then named — never cut mid-note.

model.description: The calling model, as 'provider/model' (e.g. 'anthropic/opus-5') or just 'provider'. Selects per-model observation variants; omitting it serves the default phrasing.

query.description: What you are looking for, in your own words.

ref.description: A memory:// reference to start from: a permalink, alias, title, path, memory:// URL, or a glob like 'projects/api-*'.

timeframe.description: Only include notes at least this recent: '30d', '2w', '12h', or an ISO date. Empty means no time limit.

capture.description:
A palaia memory vault.

Save something you (the assistant) learned this session — a decision, a preference, a correction, a fact worth keeping — as an uncurated inbox/ note (format spec §7). No placement decision is needed; the curator later files, deduplicates and structures it. An identical capture is acknowledged with duplicate=true and not written again. For notes the user explicitly asked for, use write/edit instead.

content.description: Required. The knowledge itself, understandable without this conversation.

source.description: Where this came from. Defaults to 'agent capture, <date>'.

what_it_concerns.description: Required. The topic or entity this is about; becomes the note title, e.g. 'API Gateway'.

why_keep.description: Required. Why it is worth keeping — what goes wrong if it is forgotten.

delete.description:
A palaia memory vault.

Delete a note by permalink. Irreversible outside git history. A reference that matches no note returns deleted=false, not an error.

permalink.description: The note's permalink (alias, exact title or path also work).

edit.description:
A palaia memory vault.

Update an existing note. `body` replaces the whole body; `append` adds text on a new line after the (possibly replaced) body; `tags` replaces the full tag list. Omitted fields keep their current value.

append.description: Text appended on a new line after the body.

body.description: New body, replacing the current one.

permalink.description: The note's permalink (alias, exact title or path also work).

tags.description: New tags, replacing the whole list.

inbox_status.description:
A palaia memory vault.

Inbox health: how many uncurated captures are waiting, the oldest entry's age, and the most recent capture.

list.description:
A palaia memory vault.

List note summaries (permalink, title, type, tags, folder, modified — no bodies), sorted by permalink. With `folder`, only notes directly in that folder are listed (subfolders are not included). `meta` notes are excluded.

folder.description: Vault folder, e.g. 'projects/api'. Empty means the vault root (write/move) or the whole vault (list); for list the match is exact, subfolders excluded.

move.description:
A palaia memory vault.

Move a note to a different folder. Its permalink never changes.

folder.description: Vault folder, e.g. 'projects/api'. Empty means the vault root (write/move) or the whole vault (list); for list the match is exact, subfolders excluded.

permalink.description: The note's permalink (alias, exact title or path also work).

read.description:
A palaia memory vault.

Read one note in full. `permalink` also accepts the note's alias, exact title or vault path; an unknown or ambiguous reference is an error. The text result shows value references resolved to their current values; structured_content.body is the note as written — use that as the base for edit.

permalink.description: The note's permalink (alias, exact title or path also work).

recall.description:
A palaia memory vault.

Recall what matters about a topic or a specific note. Prefer this over search when you want to *use* what the vault knows: results are ranked by relevance plus recency, how often they are used, and how load-bearing they are; shared values are resolved to their current source; and rules phrased per model family arrive already narrowed to yours. Pass a query, or a ref (permalink/title/memory:// URL/glob) when you know the address.

limit.description: How many results to return, best first.

model.description: The calling model, as 'provider/model' (e.g. 'anthropic/opus-5') or just 'provider'. Selects per-model observation variants; omitting it serves the default phrasing.

query.description: What you are looking for, in your own words.

ref.description: A memory:// reference to start from: a permalink, alias, title, path, memory:// URL, or a glob like 'projects/api-*'.

recall_pick.description:
A palaia memory vault.

App-only helper for the recall-explorer UI: fetch the full content of one or more search/recall results the user selected, so only those enter the model's context — SPEC-208's selective-context mechanism, not a general-purpose batch-read tool.

refs.description: References of the notes to load; the call fails on the first one that does not resolve.

recent_activity.description:
A palaia memory vault.

The most recently modified notes, most recent first, up to `limit`. Summaries only (no bodies); `meta` notes are excluded.

limit.description: Maximum results to return, best or most recent first.

review_decide.description:
A palaia memory vault.

App-only action for the review-queue UI: approve or reject one curator proposal, flipping its frontmatter `status` (format spec §8) — the exact same effect as doing so in the dashboard or by editing the note directly. Only valid on a proposal whose status is currently 'proposed'.

permalink.description: Permalink of a proposal whose status is 'proposed'.

review_queue.description:
A palaia memory vault.

List every curator maintenance proposal awaiting review (format spec §8) — the review-queue app's data source. Each proposal is a card: title, status, and its full body (a human-readable explanation, sometimes with a diff/plan).

search.description:
A palaia memory vault.

Search this vault's notes. Returns best matches first. Each hit reports which retrieval channel found it ('text' = full-text/BM25, 'meaning' = semantic/vector, both = found by both) plus that channel's rank; the result reports the search mode that actually ran and whether it was degraded (e.g. semantic search unavailable, answered from full-text alone) — weigh the hits accordingly.

limit.description: Maximum results to return, best or most recent first.

write.description:
A palaia memory vault.

Create a new note the user asked for, at `<folder>/<slugified title>.md`. If a note already exists at that path the call fails rather than overwriting — search first and edit the existing note instead. Knowledge you picked up yourself goes through capture.

folder.description: Vault folder, e.g. 'projects/api'. Empty means the vault root (write/move) or the whole vault (list); for list the match is exact, subfolders excluded.

tags.description: Tags to set. Omit for none.

title.description: Note title; also sets the file name (slugified).

type.description: Frontmatter type. Default 'note'; 'meta' notes are hidden from search, list and recent_activity.
